title: Major Microsoft Outlook Outage Leaves People With Email Jobs Unable to Email
gist: Microsoft 365 suffered a major multi-hour outage on Thursday affecting Exchange Online/Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot 365 and Defender XDR across the Americas; Microsoft attributed it to servers failing automated health checks rather than traffic or a cyberattack, and the root cause remained unclear.

themes.theme: Scope and timeline of the Microsoft 365 outage

insights.claim: Microsoft 365 business and enterprise services suffered a major outage on Thursday, starting with Microsoft Teams issues in North America around 10:40 am ET and expanding to Exchange Online mailbox access problems across the Americas by about 1 pm ET.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Highlights concentration risk in a core enterprise SaaS dependency for millions of businesses.

insights.claim: Microsoft said impacted services during the outage may include Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Copilot 365, and Microsoft Defender XDR.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Simultaneous failure of productivity, AI and security products shows correlated risk in bundled cloud suites.
insights.locator: In an update on its status page

insights.claim: Downdetector outage reports for Outlook and other Microsoft 365 products spiked around noon ET and began falling around 1:15 pm ET.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Third-party uptime trackers provide real-time signals on service reliability incidents.
insights.locator: Outage reports on the service uptime

insights.claim: Microsoft said the connectivity errors were tied to servers going offline and failing automated health checks, not to increased traffic, though elevated load across multiple regions was likely contributing.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Infrastructure-side failure rather than demand surge points to internal reliability/ops issues.
insights.quote: a problem” was “causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable
insights.locator: It is currently unclear when the outage

insights.claim: To mitigate the outage, Microsoft paused all deployments, redistributed connection traffic across its broader worldwide infrastructure, and restarted affected servers.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Pausing deployments suggests a possible change-related trigger and shows standard incident playbooks.

insights.claim: There was no indication that a cyberattack caused the Microsoft outage; cloud outages commonly stem from configuration errors, DNS resolution issues, or cyberattacks.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Distinguishing ops failures from security incidents matters for assessing reputational and liability exposure.
insights.locator: Outages in cloud services occur frequently

themes.theme: Historical precedent for large cloud outages

insights.claim: Major Microsoft outages are relatively rare but not unprecedented: in July 2024 a corrupted CrowdStrike update crashed Windows machines worldwide, while a separate, nearly simultaneous Azure outage knocked out services for hours and caused untold millions in lost revenue.
insights.speaker: Andrew Couts
insights.so_what: Recurring large-scale outages underscore systemic single-vendor risk for enterprises and potential demand for resilience/multi-cloud.
insights.locator: While major Microsoft outages are relatively rare
